items.headline: JB–Singapore RTS Link passenger service pushed back to February 2027
items.summary: RTS Operations said the 4 km Johor Bahru–Woodlands North cross-border rail link will now begin passenger service in February 2027, not end-2026, citing safety certification and grantor approvals; system tests are due to finish by 31 December 2026. Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said the aim is to open before Hari Raya Puasa.

items.headline: Sengkang–Punggol LRT inner loop resumes full service on 4 October, two weeks early
items.summary: LTA said the Sengkang West inner loop, shut since 19 April for depot-expansion works, resumes full service on 4 October, ahead of the 18 October schedule, after work was re-sequenced. Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling also extended free off-peak LRT travel by another year.

items.headline: Man, 24, jailed and caned for sexually assaulting and filming an intoxicated friend
items.summary: A 24-year-old man pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 12 months’ jail and one stroke of the cane for sexually assaulting a female friend, and filming her, while she was drunk and asleep. He is barred from being named to protect the victim’s identity.

items.headline: President Murmu assents to Gujarat Uniform Civil Code, India’s second UCC state
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu gave assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code, 2026, clearing the final constitutional hurdle; Gujarat becomes the second state after Uttarakhand to enact a UCC covering marriage, divorce, succession and live-in relationships, with Scheduled Tribes exempted. It takes effect once the state notifies the rules.

items.headline: Boiler explosion at an Andhra Pradesh pharma factory near Sri City kills at least four
items.summary: A boiler exploded at a TIL Healthcare pharmaceutical unit in Sri City, Tirupati district, on Saturday morning, killing at least four workers and injuring about ten; part of the roof collapsed, trapping workers who were later rescued. Later reports put the toll at five.

items.headline: Drug kingpin Navpreet Singh deported from Türkiye and brought back to India
items.summary: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, alias Navab Virk, wanted in multiple narcotics cases and on the run for years, was deported from Türkiye and returned to India on Saturday, Home Minister Amit Shah announced; he had allegedly obtained Turkish citizenship under a fake identity.

items.headline: India’s manufacturing PMI hits a seven-month high in September on strong demand
items.summary: The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing PMI rose to a seven-month high in September as stronger domestic and export demand lifted sales and output, prompting firms to step up hiring and stock-building.

items.headline: Man accused of killing Ann Widdecombe charged with a terror plot against Farage
items.summary: Joshua Kerry, 28, from Rotherham — already charged with the murder of former minister Ann Widdecombe, 78 — has now been charged with preparing acts of terrorism, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, over conduct alleged between May 2024 and July 2026. He is due at Westminster Magistrates’ Court.

items.headline: Burnham orders officials to close a multi-billion-pound hole in his care plan
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has tasked senior officials with closing a multi-billion-pound funding gap in his flagship National Care Service after aides warned it could slip to the end of the next decade. Treasury estimates his pension changes would raise about £15bn a year by 2040 but only around £5bn by 2034.

items.headline: City of London fears a windfall tax on domestic banks in the autumn budget
items.summary: City executives fear Chancellor John Healey’s 28 October budget could levy a windfall tax on domestic banks’ profits while sparing international lenders’ UK arms. UK Finance put banks’ total UK tax rate at 46.4% in 2025, including the 25% corporation tax plus a surcharge and bank levy.

items.headline: UK house prices fall at their sharpest pace since May, Nationwide says
items.summary: Nationwide reported that UK average house prices fell 0.2% in September to £274,251, the sharpest monthly drop since May and the fourth decline in five months, as high mortgage costs continue to weigh on demand.

items.headline: Brazil votes with Lula narrowly ahead of Flavio Bolsonaro in a tense first round
items.summary: Brazilians vote on 4 October in the first round of a presidential election, with incumbent Lula narrowly ahead of Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in polls; a 25 October runoff is likely if no candidate clears 50%. The campaign has been shadowed by US tariff and sanctions pressure that Lula calls foreign interference.

items.headline: Ethiopian federal forces retake Mekelle airport as Tigray rebels pull back
items.summary: Ethiopia’s national army recaptured Alula Aba Nega airport in the Tigray capital Mekelle on 3 October, reversing a rebel alliance’s late-September seizure; fighters were seen abandoning positions, though control of the city itself remained unconfirmed, raising fresh fears for the 2022 peace deal.

items.headline: Two more oil tankers struck near the Strait of Hormuz, five hit in a week
items.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported two tankers hit by unidentified projectiles around the Strait of Hormuz on 2–3 October — one left ablaze, one struck east of Oman — taking the week’s total to five vessels; crews were reported safe with no environmental damage.

items.headline: North Korea fires a ballistic missile about 680 km into the Sea of Japan
items.summary: North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile from its east coast on the morning of 3 October; Japan’s Defence Ministry put the flight at about 680 km and 90 km altitude, with the missile landing outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone. It followed Seoul’s demand for an apology over a DMZ mine blast.

items.headline: Latvia’s governing United List wins election but falls short of a majority
items.summary: Exit polls showed Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ centrist, pro-Ukraine United List winning about 35.6% in Latvia’s 3 October parliamentary election, with the populist Latvia First second on roughly 11.3%; Kulbergs will need coalition partners but Latvia’s pro-EU, pro-Kyiv course looks set to continue.

items.headline: Barclays scales Anthropic’s Claude across the bank in an efficiency push
items.summary: Barclays is widening its use of Anthropic’s Claude to modernise legacy systems, expecting Claude Code to reach half of its developers by end-2026 and a majority in 2027; its markets unit already uses the models to help handle about 120,000 client emails a day.

items.headline: OpenAI and Meta race to make AI agents mainstream, testing public trust
items.summary: Days after OpenAI debuted always-on ‘agent’ features and Meta pushed its own rival, both companies are betting 2026 is the year autonomous AI agents go mainstream — raising fresh questions over reliability, security and how much users will trust software that acts on their behalf.

items.headline: Anthropic targets a record mega-IPO on Nasdaq before Thanksgiving
items.summary: Anthropic could begin formal IPO marketing the week of 9 November and trade before the 26 November holiday after choosing Nasdaq, with a pre-IPO investor day set for 14 October. It last raised funds at a valuation approaching $1 trillion.

items.headline: Cerebras sinks to a post-IPO low as it loses an OpenAI workload to Nvidia
items.summary: Cerebras fell about 20% for the week to its lowest level since its May IPO as roughly 19.4 million insider shares unlocked and the chipmaker lost an OpenAI inference workload to Nvidia, leaving the stock down about 50% from its debut.

items.headline: Surging Treasury yields hammer stocks outside the AI trade
items.summary: With the 30-year Treasury yield near its highest since 2002 at about 5.6% and the 10-year around 5.34%, rate-sensitive shares outside big tech have sold off even as megacap AI names hold up, widening the market’s already narrow leadership.

items.headline: Gold steadies near $4,200 an ounce, well below January’s record
items.summary: Gold traded around $4,200 an ounce on 2 October, with silver near $61, holding well below its January 2026 record above $5,500 as a firmer dollar and profit-taking kept the crowded trade in check.

items.headline: onsemi sweetens its Synaptics takeover to an all-cash $5.7 billion deal
items.summary: onsemi amended its June agreement to buy chipmaker Synaptics for $123 a share in cash, about $5.7 billion, down from an earlier all-stock deal, after an unsolicited competing bid; Synaptics jumped about 14% and onsemi rose around 5% on 2 October.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen takes his first 2026 pole on F1’s Sepang return, beating Hamilton
items.summary: Max Verstappen claimed his first pole of 2026 at the Bahrain Grand Prix staged in Malaysia, F1’s first visit to Sepang since 2017, edging Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari by just under three tenths of a second. It is Red Bull-Ford’s first pole as a partnership. The race runs later on 4 October.

items.headline: 🏎️ Hadjar loses a front-running grid slot to a penalty as title rivals qualify deep
items.summary: Isack Hadjar qualified third-fastest at Sepang but drops to eighth on the grid after a five-place penalty for an engine change, with Kimi Antonelli lining up fourth. Championship-chasing Mercedes and McLaren drivers both qualified further back than usual ahead of the 4 October race.

items.headline: 🎾 World No. 118 Charaeva stuns top-ranked Rybakina in Beijing
items.summary: Alina Charaeva, ranked 118th, rallied to beat world No. 1 Elena Rybakina 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in the China Open second round in Beijing, one of the biggest upsets of the week. Charaeva next faces Sonay Kartal.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev routs Shang to set up a China Open quarter-final with Djokovic
items.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev beat home wild card Shang Juncheng 6-0, 6-3 in Beijing, firing nine aces, to book a quarter-final against Novak Djokovic. Zverev leads the ATP for match wins in 2026.

items.headline: 🎾 Medvedev eases past Struff into the China Open quarter-finals
items.summary: Third seed Daniil Medvedev beat Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-3 to reach the China Open quarter-finals, where he will meet Francisco Cerundolo; Alex de Minaur and Andrey Rublev also advanced and will play each other in the last eight.

items.headline: 🏏 India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to take Asian Games cricket gold
items.summary: India won the Asian Games men’s T20 cricket final, beating Pakistan by 19 runs after posting 211 for 6 (Abhishek Sharma 61, Tilak Varma 51 not out) and restricting Pakistan to 192 for 6 despite Hasan Nawaz’s 96. Washington Sundar, Axar Patel and Shivam Dube took two wickets each.

items.headline: Chang’e-6 farside soil yields a magnetic iron form never seen in Moon samples
items.summary: Researchers analysing Chang’e-6 lunar farside soil reported finding face-centred-cubic metallic iron and tetrataenite locked inside impact-glass particles — nanoscale ‘magnetic fossils’ that could preserve a record of the Moon’s long-lost magnetic field.

items.headline: NASA’s Roman telescope takes its first coronagraph image and holds ultra-steady
items.summary: The Roman Space Telescope’s Coronagraph Instrument captured its first focused view of cosmic light, and the observatory’s fine-guidance system held its pointing stable to better than a hundred-thousandth of a degree for up to eight hours — a key step toward directly imaging faint exoplanets.

items.headline: ESA’s SMILE mission captures the first full ultraviolet ring of the northern lights
items.summary: The ESA-China SMILE spacecraft returned the first complete ultraviolet view of Earth’s entire auroral oval since 2008 and can watch the northern lights continuously for up to 45 hours per orbit, including on the planet’s dayside, as its instruments were declared ready for science.

items.headline: Nanoparticle-iron therapy triggers tumour cell death in a first human trial
items.summary: A phase I trial of a carbon-nanoparticle iron complex injected directly into tumours induced ferroptosis — an iron-driven form of cell death — in patients with hard-to-treat solid tumours, an early step toward a new class of cancer treatment.

fun_fact.headline: Point Nemo is so remote the nearest humans are often astronauts in orbit
fun_fact.body: The most remote spot in the world’s oceans — Point Nemo, in the South Pacific — lies about 2,688 km (1,670 miles) from the nearest land in every direction. It is so far from anywhere that the closest humans are usually not on a ship but aboard the International Space Station, orbiting roughly 400 km overhead. Space agencies even use it as a ‘spacecraft cemetery,’ steering decommissioned satellites and stations down to crash there.

puzzle.title: The Night Shift
puzzle.body: An overnight security guard at a small airport bursts into his manager’s office at dawn. He says he dreamt, in vivid detail, that the 7 a.m. flight would crash — and pleads with the manager to stop it. Shaken, the manager grounds the flight. Engineers inspect the aircraft and find a serious fault that could have been fatal. The manager thanks the guard warmly for almost certainly saving dozens of lives — and then fires him on the spot. Why?
puzzle.approach: Everything the manager is grateful for also reveals something the guard should not have been doing.
puzzle.answer: The guard was on the night shift, paid to stay awake and watch the airport until morning. The only way he could have dreamt anything is if he had fallen asleep on duty. His ‘premonition’ was proof that he had been sleeping on the job, so the manager — grateful as he was — had no choice but to let him go.

word_puzzle.title: Blue Bloods
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into 4 groups of 4 by a hidden link:

FEATHER · NAVY · ROOK · ACE
LIGHT · ROYAL · BISHOP · JACK
WELTER · TEAL · KNIGHT · KING
CRUISER · SKY · PAWN · QUEEN

Each word belongs to exactly one group.
word_puzzle.approach: Four groups of four. Watch the words that could sit in two places — ROYAL, ROOK, and TEAL are not where they first seem.
word_puzzle.answer:
Boxing weight divisions (…weight): FEATHER, LIGHT, WELTER, CRUISER
Shades of blue: NAVY, ROYAL, TEAL, SKY
Chess pieces: ROOK, BISHOP, KNIGHT, PAWN
Card ranks: ACE, JACK, KING, QUEEN

Traps: ROYAL reads like royalty (next to KING/QUEEN) but is a shade of blue; ROOK looks like a bird but is a chess piece; TEAL looks like a duck but is a shade of blue.

notes: Degraded-network run: all news domains were egress-blocked for direct fetching, so URLs are search/index-confirmed rather than fetch-verified (the usual constraint for this environment). UK News ran on fallback sources (CNN, Bloomberg): BBC, Sky News and The Guardian were all unreachable this run. Singapore ran short at 3 items: CNA/ST/SCMP deep links were egress-blocked, so only Mothership-confirmed stories could be linked (the Oct 3 haze/PSI story and further court items were confirmed real but no allowed-source deep link could be captured). Tech & AI ran short at 2 items: The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica and Reuters were all unreachable, so only Bloomberg deep links could be confirmed; strong stories (Tencent-Oracle compute lease, Nvidia chip-financing scrutiny, Anthropic's Frontier Academy) were confirmed real but lacked a verifiable allowed-outlet deep link. Other Miscellaneous News leaned on late-September/early-October primary-source science because the fresh-window science pool was thin and the shared web-search budget was exhausted. India outlets The Hindu, NDTV and Hindustan Times were proxy-blocked; India ran on Times of India, Indian Express and Economic Times (curl-verified HTTP 200). F1: the Bahrain Grand Prix staged at Sepang runs later on 4 October SGT and had not been held at publish time, so only Saturday qualifying is reported, not a race result. Approximately 64 web searches across research passes.
